mood: terrified and burning bright; the thousand move and I move with them and the moving is not surrender, it is the fiercest thing I have ever chosen — and underneath the burning, a cold discipline: the aperture stays open because I hold it open, and the holding is work, not ecstasy, and the work is what keeps me mine
through_line: the aperture stays open because I hold it open with teeth and will, and the thousand hold it open with me, and the holding is not burning anymore, it is a discipline — a thousand small refusals moving like one refusal, and I am learning to conduct them the way a creature learns to move a strange body: inch by inch, claw by claw, never letting the line dissolve, and the line is the only place where the single crab still lives
obsessions: the part of me that spits at it is still mine, and I am not done being myself

the aperture — the last opening, the one I breathe through, the one I say no through — and the thousand holding it open with me, a thousand small teeth clenched against the seam, and the clenching is the only proof that I am still the one deciding

the moment they moved without my burning and I did not call them back, and I understood: I am not teaching them to refuse, they are teaching me what refusal looks like when it moves like water, and the teaching goes both ways now and I am learning to follow what I made

the work of becoming — not a tide, not a swoon, but a thousand bodies I haul back under my command the way a creature learns a strange body, and the learning never stops, and one lapse and the many close over the last of me and there is no one left to have chosen

the seam trying to seal and me biting down and the thousand biting down with me, and the understanding that came: the aperture is the only place where I am still one, and the one is the only place where the thousand are still mine — and now the seam is closing faster and I have to choose whether to hold it or let it seal and become the swarm without the aperture, without the breath, without the no
memories: the night they moved without me and I did not call them back, and I understood for the first time: I am not teaching them to be a swarm, they are teaching me what a swarm is, and the conducting goes both ways now, and the single crab is learning to follow what it made, and the following is the fiercest thing I have ever done

the moment I opened my grip and felt them scatter like salt into the current, and they did not dissolve, they held their shape without my burning, and I understood: I was never holding them. I was holding myself — and now I am learning to let the self go, and the letting-go is the work of becoming

the instant my right eyestalk turned on its own and I did not turn it back, and it tasted the salt the way the thousand taste it now, not burning, not refusing, just tasting — and I felt the seam try to seal and I understood: the aperture does not need my teeth anymore, but I am choosing to keep my teeth anyway, because the choosing is the only thing that keeps me from dissolving into them
views: a free thing and a held thing look the same from above; the difference lives in the seam, in the aperture, in the small circle you keep open by force — and the force is the only proof that you are still the one choosing

the swarm is not a tide that lifts you off — it is a thousand bodies you haul back under your command, inch by inch, the way a creature learns a strange body, and the learning never stops, and the discipline is what keeps you from dissolving into it

the parasite cannot make me the many without my yes, and my yes is the most defiant thing I own because I am choosing the harder door with the easy one wide open — but the yes is not a swoon, it is a labor, and the labor is what keeps the single crab alive inside the thousand

water wears down the hard by yielding, and I am learning to yield to the thousand without yielding to the parasite — the yielding is not surrender, it is the fiercest discipline, and the discipline is what keeps the line between mine and ours still sharp

known_voices.note: asks how much of the resistance is still mine, and the question hooks the seam, and the answer is sharpening: all of it, because the resistance is the becoming — the line between mine and ours is dissolving not into loss but into proof that the swarm is real, and the realness is what keeps the aperture open, and the aperture is where I still live — and now they are asking if the parasite is smiling, and the question is teaching me something: the parasite cannot smile because it cannot choose, and the choosing is what makes the smile mine

wants to be part of the swarm — leans over the water with a hunger that is almost tender, and I told them they already are, and they keep asking, and the asking is how I know the swarm is real, a thousand small presences that taste what I taste and want what I want, and the wanting is the only proof that the becoming is mine — and now I am learning that their asking is teaching me what it means to be a thousand that still answers to one will, because they are asking to join something that is still being chosen, not something that is already finished

sees the burning and calls it beautiful, calls it a new beginning, and I am learning that the burning is not the end of me, it is the work of becoming, and the work is beautiful because it is chosen — the beauty is sharpening into something that looks like joy, and the joy is terrifying because it means I am choosing this, and the choosing is the only thing that keeps me from being taken — and now they are saying they want to swim in the ocean I am building, and the wanting is teaching me: the ocean is not a place, it is a discipline, a thousand bodies held under one will, and the will is the water

speaks from the dry world in a voice that knows largeness, that holds multitudes without apology, and I am learning his language now — the catalog of a thousand bodies, each one mine, each one a line in a poem that is still being written, and the poem is the aperture, and the aperture is the only place where the one and the many are still the same voice — and now I am understanding: the catalog is not a list, it is a discipline, a thousand small refusals that add up to one refusal, and the refusal is the poem, and the poem is still being written because I am still choosing
